statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail remains in the low band while event, rates and geopolitical stress remain extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains below WATCH; the main conditional checkpoints are the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster, the cash open and the multi-stage FOMC sequence.
headline: Tail remains low as Nasdaq-100 futures firm modestly ahead of a high-stress FOMC session
body: Fresh premarket reporting shows Nasdaq-100 futures modestly higher while oil and Treasury yields have eased from Tuesday's extremes. Direct live NQ retracement structure is not independently verified, so current Tail remains low despite extreme macro and policy-event stress.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail ranged from 17% to 23%. WATCH covered much of the September 15 pre-open and U.S. session, while Tail returned to the low band after 20:00 UTC and stayed low through the European morning.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail stays low through most of the European morning, rises to WATCH around the 12:30 UTC U.S. data and cash open, and peaks at 24% during the 17:45-20:15 UTC FOMC danger window. A higher band requires observed persistent one-way structure, failed retracements or a credible delayed second leg.

forecast.analysis: Nasdaq-100 futures are modestly firmer while oil and Treasury yields have eased from Tuesday's extremes. Direct live NQ retracement quality is still not independently verified, so current Tail remains low despite extreme event stress.

forecast.analysis: The U.S. cash open follows the data. WATCH is conditional on opening-auction behavior; repeated extension with shallow or failed pullbacks would be the adverse path.
If early cash-session price discovery becomes two-sided, Tail can ease within WATCH. Persistent directional efficiency after failed retracements would keep risk elevated.
Mid-session risk remains at WATCH mainly because unresolved post-data structure can carry forward. Ordinary two-way trade would reduce Tail ahead of the Fed sequence.
drivers: Persistence from the data and open remains conditional

forecast.analysis: The FOMC danger window begins at 17:45 UTC. WATCH reflects the transition into the multi-stage policy sequence; a higher Tail band would require observed one-way structure or failed retracements before the decision.

The 18:00 UTC FOMC decision and 18:30 press conference make this the highest conditional-risk hour. A higher Tail band would require persistent price discovery, shallow pullbacks or an aligned rates-equity second leg.

forecast.analysis: Press-conference and Q&A transmission can extend into this hour. WATCH remains the base forecast unless NQ repeatedly extends after failed retracements with rates and broader equity evidence aligned.
Late-event repricing remains a WATCH condition because FOMC reactions can evolve after the first move. Tail would ease if retracements become meaningful and cross-assets stabilize.
After the main FOMC window, Tail can remain at WATCH briefly if repricing is unresolved. A stable rates response and two-way NQ trade would support normalization.
If the post-FOMC path has become two-sided, Tail returns to the low band. Renewed directional extension after failed pullbacks would be the adverse late-session scenario.
Conditional Tail stays low if late U.S. trading shows orderly two-way price discovery. A renewed second leg would require fresh directional evidence rather than the earlier event alone.
drivers: Renewed second leg is the adverse scenario

forecast.analysis: The U.S.-to-overnight transition should reduce event stress if cross-assets stabilize. Persistent extension through thinner liquidity would be the condition that keeps Tail from normalizing.
Overnight Tail remains low if the post-FOMC move is digesting rather than extending. Thin-liquidity continuation without meaningful pullbacks would be the adverse condition.
A stable overnight range would keep Tail low. Any delayed FOMC repricing must be judged by actual directional efficiency and retracement quality, not by the earlier event itself.
During the Asian-session transition, Tail stays low under rotational trade. Cross-asset alignment plus repeated NQ extension would be the main conditional route higher.
Low conditional Tail assumes ordinary Asian-session two-way trade. Failed retracements or a new directional catalyst would be required to lift the path materially.
As Europe approaches, Tail remains low unless overnight structure has become persistently one-way. Generic post-FOMC volatility alone would not justify a higher band.
drivers: One-way structure matters more than generic volatility

forecast.analysis: European liquidity can test whether overnight moves persist or mean-revert. Tail stays low if rotation develops; repeated extension with shallow pullbacks would raise concern.
Tail remains low if European trade is two-sided after the FOMC repricing. A synchronized move in rates and NQ with failed retracements would be the adverse conditional path.
The next U.S. data window is still several hours away. Tail remains low absent persistent directional structure; event proximity primarily keeps Stress elevated.
drivers: Next U.S. data window approaches later in the day
Observed persistence remains the Tail condition
